evaluations.question: Which language family shows the highest effect value for any single model configuration, and which model achieves it?
evaluations.expected_answer: IE-Indic, with XLM-B2 or mBERT-B2 reaching approximately 21-24
evaluations.model_answer: The IE-Indic language family shows the highest effect value, achieved by the XLM-R₂ model configuration, reaching approximately 24-25.

evaluations.question: For the Semitic language family, how many of the six model configurations show a negative effect value?
evaluations.expected_answer: 2-3 (some of the green bars appear to be slightly negative or near zero)
evaluations.model_answer: For the Semitic language family, approximately 3 of the six model configurations show negative effect values (mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, and XLM-B₂ appear to be at or below zero).
evaluations.reason: Answer falls within expected approximate range.

evaluations.question: Which language family has the smallest spread (range) across its six model configurations?
evaluations.expected_answer: Isolate or Uralic (both have very small bars close to 0, with a range of roughly 1-2)
evaluations.model_answer: The Isolate language family has the smallest spread across its six model configurations, with all values clustered very close to zero.

evaluations.question: In how many language families does XLM-B2 exceed or approximately equal an effect value of 15?
evaluations.model_answer: XLM-B2 exceeds or approximately equals an effect value of 15 in 3 language families: IE-Germanic (≈15), IE-Indic (≈21), and IE-Slavic (≈17). Uralic also appears close at roughly 15.
